title: The Cosmic Chess Game of the Stars
body: Hundreds of years ago, people played a magical board game based on the night sky. Instead of normal kings and pawns, the pieces represented planets, including a sad Saturn wrapped in a dark blanket. To move, players had to roll a special seven-sided die and watch how the stars aligned.

variants.lucy: Long ago in the Middle Ages, people played a beautiful game modeled after the evening sky. Instead of ordinary chess pieces, they moved tiny planets, including a sorrowful Saturn draped in a dark, cozy shawl. They watched the real stars above to see how to guide their cosmic pieces.
variants.luca: To launch their celestial armies, players had to roll a strange die with seven different sides. Every single roll sent a planet charging across the board depending on the patterns in the sky. Imagine controlling the entire cosmos with one lucky toss!
variants.cn: 很久以前的中世纪，人们玩一种照着夜空的样子做出来的美丽棋戏。棋盘上摆的不是普通的棋子，而是一颗颗小小的行星，其中还有一颗忧伤的土星，裹着一条深色的、暖暖的披肩。下棋的人会抬头看真正的星星，看看天上的星星怎么排，再决定棋盘上的星星该怎么走。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
